name: Linocut
summary: A moving linocut print: cream paper, carbon-black key plate, one misregistered pumpkin-orange spot plate and a sparing teal.
description: Everything looks carved and printed: black ink shapes with white gouge marks cut into them, black lens-shaped knife marks on bare paper, and a single orange spot colour printed slightly off-register so a sliver of paper shows on one side. There are no gradients anywhere – tone comes only from line density, carved fish-scale cuts and hatched shadows, and the land is composed of calm paper areas, clumped grass and litter drifts. Motion is printed too: figures appear when a brayer rolls them onto the paper, break apart like a split block and swap between hand-pulled variants on twos.
avoidFor: colour-coded puzzle games that need many hues
scenes packed with dozens of figures (they merge into black)

difficulty.why: Every new figure has to be designed as one solid-ink mass carved with white gouges plus one paper mass carved with black lenses, with the orange plate placed on a single focal element at a fixed offset. The white cut lines inside black areas are fine detail work, and many dark figures close together blur into one black mass unless halos and spacing are planned.

technique.resolution: Native resolution. Sprites baked at K = clamp(round(screenH/360*4)/4, 2, 5) px per world unit; ground chunks (256 units) at up to 2.5 px per unit.
technique.summary: Figures are drawn as filled ink shapes plus filled 'lens' (gouge) and 'taper' marks in paper colour or ink, the orange plate is drawn offset by (0.8, 0.55) units, then a paper halo is put behind and an ink-void pass knocks pinholes into the black. Every pose is baked twice with different jitter seeds (two 'pulls') and the pulls alternate at 6 fps.
technique.linework: No strokes of constant width: every line is a filled lens (pointed both ends, half-width 0.12-0.85 units) or a taper (blunt start, sharp tip). Outlines are thin ink strokes 0.5-0.75 units plus a heavy 'crescent' (shape minus a shrunken copy shifted to the upper left, scale 0.93-0.96) on the shadow side.
technique.shading: Two values only (ink / paper) plus flat spot colours. Shade = parallel black lenses getting wider toward the shadow side (e.g. 6 lenses widening 0.16 -> 0.44 on the right of the main character's round head), lit side = white gouges carved out of black (cloak folds, crown highlights).
technique.lighting: Fixed light from the upper left. Crescents and shadow lenses sit bottom-right, carved highlights top-left. Glows are flat orange ray stars (12-18 spikes) printed on the spot plate, never gradients.
technique.texture: Paper: 512x512 fibre map (1300 curved fibres) + mottling + grain, offset -22..+14. Ink: 256x256 void noise; where it exceeds ~238 the ink lightens 70% toward paper (pinholes). Orange gets +-6% density grain.

palette.name: Paper
palette.role: Ground, halos, carved highlights (~65% of the screen)

palette.name: Ink
palette.role: Key plate: all outlines, solid masses, marks (~30%)

palette.name: Pumpkin Orange
palette.role: The one spot plate: main character's head, glowing cores, lantern faces, collectibles, progress bar, large floating numbers (~4%)

palette.name: Teal
palette.role: Second spot, used sparingly: frost stipple on the floating creature, core ring of the large creature, centre of the large collectible (<1%)

palette.name: Ink Deep
palette.role: Hard offset shadow on cards / panels

paletteRules: Only paper, ink and flat spot colours. No gradients, no transparency effects, no soft shadows.
Orange is always printed offset by (+0.8, +0.55) world units (mirrored x with facing); teal by (-0.55, +0.45). The same offset everywhere – that is the misregistration signature.
Spot colours appear only inside holes cut in the key plate (holeSpot) or as their own plate under an ink outline.
Tone is made with line density: wider/more black lenses = darker. Never mix grey.
Teal is an accent for at most 2-3 element types.

typography.role: Titles, clock / timer, card keys – western woodtype display
typography.css: font: 400 34px/1.05 'Rye', Georgia, serif; letter-spacing: 2px; color: #1b1715; text-shadow: 2px 2px 0 #ea6820;

typography.role: Numbers: bar values, counters, badges, floating numbers, card names
typography.css: font: 400 17px 'Alfa Slab One', Georgia, serif; color: #1b1715;

typography.role: Typewriter body text and small labels
typography.css: font: 400 11px 'Special Elite', 'Courier New', monospace; letter-spacing: 3px; border-top: 2px solid #1b1715;

world.summary: Per-pixel 'ink coverage' on fibrous paper. Noise fields with signed distances define regions; each region has a carved pattern computed analytically per pixel (grass ticks, furrows, litter flecks, cobbles, solid ink with echo contours) separated by 1.5-unit paper gutters. Texture is clumped, never sprinkled: grass and litter only grow in noise-driven clumps and in drifts along region edges, leaving large calm paper areas between them.
layers: Meadow: grass ticks on a 9-unit hashed grid (1-3 tapered blades, length 2.2-3.55, half-width 0.46) only inside clumps (density 0.8 * smoothstep(0.57, 0.72, T) * smoothstep(0.4, 0.62, M)) and in an 8-unit drift along every region edge; rare 'chatter' (3-5 parallel short gouges) in the cleared paper
Field: ploughed furrows along a warped direction field (spacing 4.4 units, half-width up to 0.66) with a carved ditch line at the edge; sprouts snapped onto the furrows

Forest floor: three carved edge cuts (0.5, 2.5, 4.3 units in), a clean band, then oriented litter flecks following the flow of the land, almost bare in the open (density 0.015) and dense in drifts (up to 0.73)
Dark soil: solid ink, two paper echo contours 1.8 and 3.4 units inside the edge, oriented white gouge flecks deeper inside
Road: 22-unit-wide cobbles from Worley cells (size 4.4) with paper joints, hatched stone shading on the shadow side, curb line
Ink pass: pinhole voids (VOID noise) and paper fibres showing through the ink
Decals in clumps: flowers and pebbles in meadow clumps, mushrooms, twigs and leaves in forest drifts, bones in the soil, rare skulls, carved tree roots under every tree

characters.summary: Bold silhouettes built from filled smooth paths, two-bone tapered limbs and lens marks. Each figure mixes a paper-filled form (with black carving) and a solid-ink form (with white gouges) so it reads on both paper and dark soil. A 1.0-1.15-unit paper halo is baked behind every sprite. The main character has 8 computed walk poses, 4 breathing idle poses + a blink, a crouch, a dash and a recoil pose; each creature has 6 poses – all baked as 2 carving pulls per facing plus a negative print.
rules: Main character ~18 x 30 units: a lobed orange pumpkin head (offset orange plate, black ribs, shading lenses, heavy crescent, carved face) with a curly stem leaf, a short ragged black poncho with a V-cut hem, a paper folk zigzag band with a dot in every tooth and a stitched hem, a long striped scarf, paper mittens and two-bone legs with boots (knee from hip/ankle distance).

Walk = 8 computed poses: contact, down, passing, up for each leg; body bob 0.85*sin(2ph), lean 0.07, heel lift on the trailing foot, arms counter-swing (near hand x = 3.0 - 2.9*cos ph). Head (delay 1.0 rad), hem (1.1), stem leaf (1.6) and scarf (1.8) follow through with growing phase delays – overlapping action.

Small creature ~23 x 30: a root bulb with a solid ink crown, a carved paper rim on the lit edge, angry carved eyes and brow, a toothed grimace, root legs, root arms swinging against the legs, a curling tap root and a leafy top that swing after the body.

Fast creature ~30 x 26: a hungry sheet-spirit – paper body with teal frost stipple, hollow eyes, a wailing mouth that opens and closes, reaching claw arms that alternate, a whipping tail that breaks up into halftone dots.

Large creature ~50 x 58: a root giant – solid ink body with concentric white arc gouges, a crown of leaves, heavy arms and a glowing core (orange plate in a hole, teal ring, carved rays) that flickers between poses.
Every form has one solid black area and one paper area; faces are carved (paper lens eyes in black or black holes in paper). The orange plate goes on the single most important element per figure.
Light from the upper left of the screen: every drawer works mirrored (scale(f,1)), so the lit side is local x-sign -f; carved highlights sit there, heavy crescents on the other side.
Animation is held: poses are picked by step, carving pulls swap at 6 fps; nothing is tweened shape by shape.

props.summary: Carved scenery sprites, y-sorted with the characters, each with a paper halo and a hatched lens shadow. Trees are mostly solid ink carved with white gouges; graves, fences and haystacks are paper forms carved with black lenses. Props cluster where the land suggests them: spruces and canopy trees in forest regions, stumps and planar-carved boulders at forest edges and beside roads, lantern poles along the roads, graves in graveyard zones.
rules: Bare oak (3 variants): carved roots, trunk limb 4.4 -> 3.0, recursive branches 3 levels deep (widths x0.6), white bark gouges on the lit side, a knot hole.

Canopy tree (3 variants, one tall and narrow): ONE black canopy mass whose leaves are carved as rows of fish-scale U-cuts following the outline – dense on the lit upper left, sparse on the shadow side – over a forked trunk showing through a gap under the canopy, a few leaf points hanging from the underside.

Spruce (2 variants): 6 toothed tiers with white lenses. Stump (2): a paper cut face with carved growth rings and a check crack. Boulders (2): ink masses with a cleared top facet hatched by parallel cuts and paper gutters between stones.

Graves (round with cross, Celtic cross, slab with a carved skull), fences with a broken rail, a scarecrow with a root-bulb head, lantern poles with orange ray stars, crow posts, haystacks (paper dome with 17 converging ink lenses).
Every tree sends 4-6 carved tapered roots (9-16 units) into the ground decal layer, so trees are always grounded.
Shadows are hatched, never soft: horizontal ink lenses filling an ellipse, shifted right; tree shadow 19 x 4.6.
Prop animation is stepped: lantern rays alternate at 3.2 fps, crows open their beaks every few seconds.

effects.name: Appear: brayer print
effects.how: A registration mark (ink cross + misregistered orange copy) is set where the figure will stand; from spawnT 0.16 to 0.78 a black brayer (ink roller) rolls upward and the figure is revealed from the feet up behind it (clip rect); on contact an ink splat is stamped and the sprite squashes and recovers (sin * 0.13).

effects.name: Disappear: split block
effects.how: 0-0.12: the negative print swells (scale 1 + t*0.9); 0.12-0.27: a pre-baked cracked block with carved paper cracks; then 4-6 wedge shards with fresh paper cut edges fly out (outQuad), rise and fall (-7u + 30u^2), tumble in 10 held steps and shrink after half-way; the last quarter fades. An ink splat stays on the ground for 2.2-3.2 s and sinks away in 4 steps.

effects.name: Hit: negative print + knock-back
effects.how: For 0.16 s the creature shows its baked negative copy (paper <-> ink by luminance), squashes (0.17 * cos) and is shoved 2.4 units along the knock-back direction with one overshoot. Layered particles: a paper-white knock-out star with ink rim (0.08 s), a black lens burst (0.2 s, orange for orbiting objects), 2 ink drops and a wood chip with gravity.

effects.name: Projectile
effects.how: Orange seed plate offset by the misregistration under a black outlined seed with a carved shine (2 pulls); trail = 3 black lenses scaled in over 0.12 s; rotation snapped to 45-degree steps * 0.35.

effects.name: Orbiting lantern
effects.how: Carved bulb lantern with orange face holes on the offset plate, over a slowly rotating 14-spike orange ray star.

effects.name: Collectibles
effects.how: Small = orange 4-point star on the offset plate with an ink outline and 4 spark lenses (2 frames); large = 8-point orange star with a teal centre hole and 8 sparks. They hover on an eased, held float curve and pop in at 170%.

effects.name: Burst and glow-up
effects.how: Burst: flash star, a large lens burst, 9-16 wood chips (some orange on the large creature), 4-8 ink drops, two halftone puffs and a ground splat. Glow-up: a carved ripple ring (ink gouges with teeth + orange arc ring on the offset plate) expanding in 9 held steps, an orange lens burst, a flash and 6 orange stars.

effects.name: Dash
effects.how: One crouch frame (anticipation), then a long forward lean; the orange plate is printed twice behind the figure, 6 and 12 units back, with multiply (overprinting ink), plus two speed-lens trails and halftone puffs.

atmosphere.summary: No light simulation: light is a fixed convention from the upper left expressed by carving, glow is printed as flat orange ray stars, shadows are hatched lenses, and a ragged ink frame encloses the screen like the edge of a printed block.
rules: Fixed light from the upper left: crescents at the lower right, white gouges at the upper left, shadows shifted right.
Glow = printed rays, not light: flat orange spike stars (12-18 spikes, alternating lengths) on the offset plate.
Paper halo (0.5-0.9 units) behind every sprite – the knock-out that keeps black figures readable on dark soil and in groups.
Ink texture everywhere: pinhole voids and paper fibres in all ink, on the ground and in sprites.
Frame: ragged ink strips (thickness max(6 px, 1.1% of H), inner jagged edge every 6-18 px) plus an inner rule; no vignette.
Full-screen overlays: rgba(27,23,21,.8) with a halftone dot pattern radial-gradient(circle, rgba(240,231,210,.16) 0 1.3px, transparent 1.7px) at 8 px.

ui.summary: Letterpress HUD: paper panels with a noise texture, 3 px ink borders, hard 4 px ink offset shadows, small radii (2 px), stepped transitions. Bars are diagonal stripe fills (orange with ink rules for the wide progress bar, ink with paper rules for the short status bar). The clock sits in a double-ruled box with a 7 px hard shadow.

motion: Everything is held: carving pulls swap at 6 fps, the walk steps through 8 poses with anim * 1.3, idle breathing poses hold ~0.38 s each, with a blink every 3.4 s.
Main character walk: contact/down/passing/up per leg, bob 0.85, arms counter-swing, head/hem/leaf/scarf follow through with 1.0-1.8 rad phase delays.
Dash: a crouch frame for the first 0.035 s (anticipation), then the dash pose with orange overprint ghosts. Hurt: recoil pose (thrown back, arm up, eyes wide) and a negative-print blink at 12 Hz.

Creatures: 6 poses; the small creature steps at anim*3.2, the large at anim*2.8, the fast creature at 9 fps on its own clock; every actor has its own phase offset (seed), so crowds never move in lock-step.
Floating figures and collectibles use an eased triangle float curve quantised to 14 steps per cycle – they linger at the top and bottom, never a plain sine.
Hit reaction 0.16 s, disappearance 0.35 s (swell, crack, shards), entrance 0.45 s (registration mark, brayer, stamp-squash).
Ambient: 8 carved leaves drift across the view on the wind, tumbling through 4 poses at 8 fps.
UI transitions are stepped (steps(2) / steps(3)) like a print being swapped, never smooth.
do: Build everything from filled lenses, tapers, limbs and smooth paths – no constant-width strokes.
Give each figure one solid black mass with white carving and one paper area with black carving.
Print orange on its own plate with the same fixed offset everywhere.
Use a heavy crescent on the bottom-right and white gouges on the top-left (light from upper left).
Bake a paper halo around sprites and pinhole voids into the ink.
Hold poses and swap two carving pulls at 6 fps; drive walks from computed contact/down/passing/up poses with lagging scarf, hem and leaf.
Let grass and litter grow in clumps and along edges, and leave big areas of bare paper.
Make entrances and exits print-shop events: registration marks, brayer, stamp, split block.
dont: Don't use gradients, blur, glow or alpha-blended shading.
Don't add more spot colours; orange plus a sparing teal is the limit.
Don't register colour perfectly inside outlines – the offset sliver is the look.
Don't draw uniform hairlines or vector-clean strokes.
Don't animate smoothly with tweens on shapes or bob things on a plain sine.
Don't scatter tufts and dots evenly over the ground.
Don't put black figures on black ground without a paper halo.
performance: All character poses (main character 8 walk + 4 idle + blink + crouch + dash + recoil, creatures 6 each) x 2 pulls x 2 facings, negative copies, cracked blocks and shatter shards, props, particles and shadows are baked at init; the expensive steps are getImageData passes (inkify, invert). Ground chunks are generators that yield every 8 rows inside a 5 ms per-frame budget: an 84x84 field grid per chunk, then per-pixel analytic patterns (grass hash cells, furrows, Worley cobbles). Per frame is only drawImage of cached sprites, a clip rect per arriving figure and up to 70 ground splats.
